methods.forecast: 24-month outlook from whichever model (seasonal average, or trend plus memory, or a pretrained model if installed) had the lowest error in a rolling backtest from six past start dates; the 80% range is the backtest's own error at each lead time. case.headline: this place: moisture in the air has risen beyond its normal range, with 2 more vital signs following
case.summary: Condition: serious. 3 of 10 vital signs have changed by more than the usual year-to-year swing, led by moisture in the air.

findings.claim: Moisture in the air has risen by 0.117 g/kg per decade since 1981, a total of +0.526 g/kg, which is 3.97 times the usual year-to-year swing.
findings.why_it_matters: The change is larger than the variation people and ecosystems here are used to.

findings.claim: Air temperature has risen by 0.691 °C per decade since 1981, a total of +3.11 °C, which is 3.16 times the usual year-to-year swing.
findings.why_it_matters: That is faster than the average over the mapped world (+0.172 °C per decade).

findings.claim: Snow depth has fallen by 4.69 cm per decade since 1981, a total of −21.1 cm, which is 2.98 times the usual year-to-year swing.
findings.why_it_matters: The change is larger than the variation people and ecosystems here are used to.

findings.claim: A raindrop falling here travels about 4 km downhill and drops 406 m before it reaches sea level.
findings.why_it_matters: It shows who is downstream: what happens to water here travels along that route.

suspects.name: North Atlantic Oscillation
suspects.case_for: Precipitation here moves with it (correlation +0.276), which accounts for about 8% of the month-to-month swings. It currently stands at −0.28.
suspects.case_against: It explains swings from year to year, not the long-term trend: trends were removed before correlating, and a correlation is not proof of cause.

suspects.name: Indian Ocean Dipole
suspects.case_for: Moisture in the air here moves with it (correlation −0.211), which accounts for about 4% of the month-to-month swings. It currently stands at +0.146.
suspects.case_against: It explains swings from year to year, not the long-term trend: trends were removed before correlating, and a correlation is not proof of cause.

suspects.name: Global warming
suspects.case_for: The planet as a whole is warming by 0.211 °C per decade, and this place is warming with it.
suspects.case_against: Global warming sets the background; how much of the local rate is due to local factors (land use, irrigation, a growing city) cannot be told from one grid cell.

case.outlook: Snow depth has the most predictable outlook: the next 12 months are expected to average 51.7 cm (80% range 40.6 to 62.9), −11.0 against the 1991–2020 average. Tested on the past, that method was 27% more accurate than assuming a normal year. For 5 other vital signs no method beat assuming a normal year.

A documented change in the observing system at the time a trend begins.
A longer record showing the change to be one phase of a slow natural cycle.

methods.trend: Theil-Sen slope on monthly anomalies; Mann-Kendall test with autocorrelation correction (larger of Hamed-Rao 1998 and AR(1) effective sample size); Benjamini-Hochberg across vital signs.
methods.early_warning: Lag-1 autocorrelation and variance in a sliding 10-year window on detrended anomalies; Kendall tau judged against 500 phase-randomised surrogates.
methods.forecast: 24-month outlook from whichever model (seasonal average, or trend plus memory, or a pretrained model if installed) had the lowest error in a rolling backtest from six past start dates; the 80% range is the backtest's own error at each lead time. The record ends in December 2025, so the outlook starts in January 2026.
methods.suspects: Best lagged correlation (mode leading by 0-6 months) of detrended anomalies with NOAA climate indices; effective sample size; Bonferroni over lags and Benjamini-Hochberg over all pairs.
caveats: Values come from a reanalysis (a weather model constrained by observations), not from a single instrument. Changes in the observing system over the decades can leave artificial steps, especially in precipitation and soil wetness.
One grid cell covers roughly 50 km, so local features such as a city or a valley are averaged out.
An early-warning signal is a statistical warning sign, not a prediction of collapse.
A correlation with a climate mode identifies a suspect, not a proven cause.
